text.p: Hong Kong hotelier Shangri-La Asia Ltd said on Thursday it had an occupancy rate of above 90 percent in October and around 80 percent in September.
"October is a very strong month," financial controller Frankie Heng told reporters at a DBS Securities seminar.
"The (room) rates in the second half are higher than the first half," he added.
Managing director Paul Bush said the company was doing "extraordinarily well" in Hong Kong "and we envisage to do equally well or better next year in Hong Kong".
Hong Kong contributed 35 percent of the group's earnings in the first half of 1996.
In mid-August, Shangri-La Asia reported interim net profit of HK$502.48 million in the six months ended June 30, up from HK$367.81 million during the same period of 1995.

Bush said the company had lodged an expression of interest in the Mass Transit Railway Corp's (MTRC) hotel development at Tai Kok Tsui, one of the main stations on the underground line being built to Hong Kong's new Chek Lap Kok Airport.
"Of course many others also expressed interest in that development and MTR will shortlist and then we go to the next stage," he said, adding that the tender stage would be in March.
"We would be quite keen to have another property in Hong Kong."
